title: Directive-first runtime refactor - directives as projections of enforcement
description: EPIC BRIEF. Objective: refactor the agent-directive system so directives are projections of enforcement rather than a parallel rule engine, harden the done-gate so declared gates are mechanically checked at closeout, and fix executor context fidelity so the full spec reaches executing agents. Motivation: the 2026-07-01 accountability audit (see sources) found (a) the directive registry appliesTo matcher re-encodes facts the runtime already derives, requiring a 382-line health checker to keep two rule systems coherent, (b) WorkItemView drops description, acceptanceCriteria, sourceRefs and parentId so executors never receive the spec (packages/ui-model/src/work-view.ts lines 107-138), (c) closeout gates validate record shape not truth because evidence outcome and command are self-asserted strings never executed or matched (packages/evidence-engine/src/evidence.ts lines 44-73). Target end state: every enforcement point emits typed gap codes; the registry is a flat gap-code to instruction+nextCommand lookup; severity taxonomy collapses to blocking, required, advisory; RequiredCloseoutGate gains declaredCommand and expectedObservable matched at close; bwrk next collapses the bundle to one executable directive so the agent loop is run-next-repeat. Constraints: preserve the directive safety boundary (instruction text only from the checked-in registry, untrusted content only in quoted data slots per docs/architecture/AGENT_DIRECTIVES.md); all schema changes additive; CLI JSON envelopes stay stable or version. Out of scope: tier-2 execute-at-close gates ship as a policy-gated draft only; epic and phase work kinds; two-actor verification. Done: all five sprint containers closed with checkpoint evidence, bwrk next drives a fixture agent loop end to end, doctor --strict passes.
